issues.description: Specification incoherence: check name, metadata, code, and CHANGELOG disagree on what is being verified
issues.detail: The PR title says 'detect VMs with multiple network interfaces.' The check file is named compute_instance_single_network_interface. The CHANGELOG entry says compute_instance_single_network_interface. The docstring promises PASS/MANUAL/FAIL outcomes including a MANUAL branch for GKE. The metadata.json description and notes describe a simple multi-NIC failure, with no mention of GKE-as-MANUAL whatsoever. An author who cannot state a single, stable postcondition for their check has not reasoned about it; they have merely typed it. Pick one specification and make every artifact agree, or refuse.

issues.description: SMUGGLED-GOTO: GKE exception encoded as a name-prefix string match
issues.detail: The check distinguishes GKE-managed instances by instance.name.startswith('gke-'). This is not a property of the resource being audited; it is a folk heuristic dressed up as a predicate. A user can name any VM 'gke-foo' and silently downgrade a FAIL to a MANUAL, defeating the very property the check exists to enforce. The precondition 'this instance is GKE-managed' is not implied by 'name starts with gke-'. Either query an authoritative signal (instance metadata, labels such as goog-gke-node, managed instance group membership) or do not make the exception at all. As written, this is a security check that can be bypassed by rename.

issues.description: The interface_count == 0 case is unreasoned and silently reports PASS
issues.detail: The else branch handles 'no network interfaces' by setting status_extended but leaves report.status as the default 'PASS' initialized at the top. The author never states whether a zero-interface instance is compliant, non-applicable, or impossible. If it is impossible, the branch should not exist or should raise. If it is possible, calling it PASS is a lie: the postcondition 'instance has exactly one NIC' is false. State the precondition (can interface_count ever be zero?) and handle it deliberately, not by falling through.

issues.description: TESTED-NOT-PROVED: no test exercises the zero-NIC branch
issues.detail: Six tests are provided; none constructs an Instance with network_interfaces=[]. The branch is reachable (the default value of the field is []), it produces a user-visible status, and it is unverified. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence — and here testing does not even attempt the third arm of a three-arm conditional. Add a test, or remove the branch.

issues.description: Mutable default argument on Pydantic model field
issues.detail: Instance.network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = [] uses a mutable default. Pydantic BaseModel typically copies defaults on instantiation, so this is usually safe in practice — but the surrounding model already uses Field-less mutable defaults elsewhere, and the pattern propagates a hazard. State the invariant: every Instance has its own list. Use Field(default_factory=list) and remove ambiguity rather than relying on framework behavior that is not asserted in the code.

issues.description: interface_names computed unconditionally for a message used only on some branches
issues.detail: interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces] is built for every instance regardless of branch. Minor; only noted because the rest of the function is a three-way conditional whose data dependencies should be made explicit at each arm. The cost is trivial; the discipline is not.

issues.description: split('/')[-1] on network/subnetwork URLs without stating the precondition
issues.detail: The service code reduces 'projects/X/global/networks/Y' to 'Y' by splitting on '/'. This is correct for current GCP URL shapes but the precondition (the field is either empty or a slash-delimited URL whose last segment is the name) is nowhere stated. A future API surface that returns short names would silently change behavior. State the invariant or use the documented URL parser.

issues.description: Docstring lists a MANUAL outcome that the metadata.json does not acknowledge
issues.detail: The class docstring documents PASS/MANUAL/FAIL with the GKE carve-out. The metadata's Description, Risk, and Notes describe a binary single-vs-multiple property and mention GKE only as an informational footnote. A reviewer reading metadata.json cannot derive the check's actual behavior. Documentation that disagrees with code is worse than no documentation.

review.summary: UNREASONED. The artifacts disagree about what is being checked: title, filename, metadata, docstring, and CHANGELOG present at least three different specifications, with a GKE MANUAL branch invented in code but absent from metadata. The GKE carve-out is a SMUGGLED-GOTO — a security predicate decided by string prefix on a user-controlled name, trivially bypassable by rename. The zero-interface branch is TESTED-NOT-PROVED and falls through to PASS by accident rather than by reasoning. The implementation works for the happy paths covered by tests, but the author cannot state a single coherent postcondition, and that is the disqualifying defect. REFUSED until the specification is made coherent across all artifacts, the GKE exception is replaced with an authoritative signal or removed, and the zero-NIC case is handled deliberately.
